name: Carbimazole

overview.mechanism: Converted to thiamazole (methimazole), which suppresses thyroid-hormone synthesis.
uses: Hyperthyroidism; the cited UK product also covers preparation for thyroid surgery and treatment around radioiodine.

paragraphs.text: The cited UK SmPC requires laboratory confirmation of hyperthyroidism and adjustment against serial thyroid-function results. It notes that renal or hepatic disease may prolong half-life, but does not provide a numeric renal-dose table or dialysis schedule. Urinary elimination of metabolites alone cannot establish either.

Agranulocytosis can be fatal. The SmPC instructs patients with fever, sore throat, mouth ulcers, bruising or bleeding to stop treatment and seek urgent medical assessment; immediate white-cell testing is indicated. Hepatic symptoms also require prompt withdrawal and investigation.

Previous carbimazole- or thiamazole-associated acute pancreatitis is a contraindication; recurrence can occur faster on re-exposure. Pregnancy requires individual benefit–risk assessment, the lowest effective dose without thyroid-hormone replacement, and close maternal, fetal and neonatal monitoring.

sources.citation: Flamingo Pharma (UK) Ltd. Carbimazole 10 mg tablets, UK SmPC; updated 25 November 2025. International product reference.

draft_notes: International reference sources do not establish the current Philippine-approved product instructions. No unsupported dialysis regimen added.
